status: Local development model in the working tree. Not a release: version unchanged, nothing installed, published or signed for distribution, nothing listened to. Five independent reviews have been through it (engine, integration, listening by measurement, behaviour, editor). The owner's decisions are applied: the name Fathom and the accent #2F7FE0, Ocean's linear Mix, a voice seed of its own for every instance, the reference's level stage and clipper kept, and the editor (a Character drop-down over the description of the selected Character and the Evolution knob). build-ebb/listening-build-01.json describes the frozen build of this revision; it is not installed.

limits: Macro 0 is exact at the depth of the nulls; above Macro 0 the model is exact only up to the random voice phase, and the phase itself agrees statistically.

Controls that move were never measured in the reference; every glide and crossfade is Fathom's own. While Size glides the lines pass through fractional lengths and the pitch bends, as in the other Characters.
The first 2.2 s of a reference instance are not modelled; Fathom starts at its settled laws with empty lines. The reference passes the dry input for about 16 ms and is brighter for half a second.
Freeze is Ocean's hold, not the reference's; its top wears down and, at Evolution above 0, its level follows the voices.
Every other control of the reference is fixed at neutral: Brightness, input filter, Transients, Ducking above 0 %, Return, Master, other Macro modes.

The reference's level stage (its Ducking at 0 %) and its output clipper are kept as parts of Fathom, by the owner's decision. The clipper acts behind the Mix: with Mix below 100 % a dry signal above +8 dBFS is turned down in Fathom and in no other Character (dry alone at a peak of 4.0: Mix 0 % leaves Default at 4.000 and Fathom at 3.623, -0.86 dB).

Every instance of the plug-in draws a voice seed of its own and keeps it for its lifetime, not in its state. An open instance repeats its movement at every restart of processing, where the reference never repeats; a reopened project, a duplicated track and an export rendered in an instance of its own get another movement. Two instances on the same steady noise correlate at 0.52 to 0.57 and sum to +4.8 to +5.0 dB over one (the reference: 0.56 and +4.9 dB); at Evolution 0 they return the same samples.
Decay below 0.5 s, Size scale below 0.3 and host rates below 44.1 kHz are outside the reference's measured range and checked against the model only.
Host rates outside 22.05 to 384 kHz are processed as the nearest bound: time and pitch scale.

Converter clock signs are measured at 48, 56, 64, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192 and 384 kHz and simulated elsewhere; the simulation gives the measured pair at seven of those rates and a wrong output clock at 56 kHz, so an unmeasured rate may be off (a null of about -77 dB instead of -117 dB, not audible).
Entering Fathom crossfades over 200 ms into an engine that starts from silence; the tail of the Character left behind fades out, and leaving Fathom fades into the FDN's live tail.

Fathom's Mix is Ocean's linear law (dry 1 - m, wet m), not the reference's: against the reference at the same percentage the wet lies 6.02 dB lower up to 50 % and the dry 6.02 dB lower from 50 % on; the two agree at 0 and at 100 % only. The reference's clipper follows the Mix, so below Mix 100 % a dry signal above +8 dBFS is turned down in Fathom and in no other Character.
Low Cut and High Damping are out of the circuit only at their end stops; one step away the decay time steps by 1 to 5 %.
Fathom's engine and level stage read the input up to +18 dBFS, the other Characters up to +12 dBFS; the dry signal in the Mix is bounded at +12 dBFS in every Character.

Low Cut, High Damping, Focus, Harmony and Mono Safe are Ocean's own and act on Fathom at Ocean's defaults (Low Cut 80 Hz, High Damping 9 kHz, Focus 100 %): the tail at 125 Hz lasts half as long, the top 30 to 46 % shorter, the wet 1.8 dB lower under steady noise.
Fathom's wet lies 4.6 to 6.3 dB below Default's under steady noise; the levels are not matched.
A VST3 automation lane of Character written by 0.21.0 plays Current for Veil and Fathom for Current; a project saved with Fathom opens as Current in 0.21.0.

The engine's signals settle at 1e-30: its output equals that of the engine without the floor on its filters wherever a sample lies above 1.3e-23. The dry share of a settled Fathom passes down to 1.2e-38 where the other Characters flush everything under 1e-20; nothing of it is audible.

The engine must be compiled without contraction: CMake passes -ffp-contract=off for its sources and fast-math is refused; the GCC and MSVC branches of the pragma were never compiled. The sum of Ocean's Mix lies outside the engine: below Mix 100 % the last bit of Fathom's output depends on whether a build fuses its product (arm64) or not (x86_64), as for the other Characters.

Known residue of the model: comb tap changes one sample off in a few percent of crossings (steady material at -80 to -93 dB at Macro 100 %), a loop lag of 2e-7 samples per pass, the last place of the oscillators' sine.
Built and run on macOS arm64 with Apple clang only; an x86_64 build was run under Rosetta.

The editor was checked in the test executable's own window on macOS only: no host, no mouse interaction, no VoiceOver; its line breaks and the walk of the keyboard were never run with the Windows or Linux font and window system.

Small text in Fathom's accent is under 4.5 : 1 (a toggle that is on: 4.21 : 1), and labels outside the description block lose their ground over bright passages of the GPU background (EVOLUTION: a glyph pixel under 4.5 : 1 in 15 % of frames at factory settings, by the editor review).
Space on the Character drop-down opens its list; the drop-down has the keyboard as soon as the editor's window has it.
The plug-in holds the date and time of its build, so a clean rebuild of the same sources has other hashes; the frozen build is the one whose hashes the manifest holds.
notRun: No listening test; no DAW; no plug-in validator (auval, pluginval, clap-validator).
AU and CLAP were built but not rendered; only the VST3 went through the Analyzer.
No Windows or Linux build, no GCC or MSVC compile of the engine.
ctest in the sanitizer build: both tests exceed its time limits (420 s and 30 s) under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer in a Debug build; the executables were run directly instead.
The plug-in was not scored statistically at Macro 50 % and its level cycle was not measured on its own.
No capture-based null at 176.4 kHz, with the plug-in at Decay above 7.3 s (the engine: up to 20 s), with the plug-in at 64, 192 or 384 kHz, or with the engine on steady material at Macro 100 %.

Above Macro 0 the built VST3 was not compared with the engine to the bit through the Analyzer: no renderer knows the seed an instance drew, and the plug-in cannot be told one. The state tests make that comparison with the seed the processor reports. The plug-in takes no phase either, so it cannot be nulled against the reference there.
That two processes without system entropy draw different seeds rests on the clock and was not run; the seed's source was tested in one process on one machine.
The renderers built with -ffp-contract=fast and for x86_64 were not compared with the Release renderer again; the engine's sources are unchanged.

The editor was not opened in a host; the live pictures come from the test executable.

decisionsForTheOwner: VST3 automation of Character: an existing lane plays Current for Veil (0.75) and Fathom for Current (1.0). Accept and note it in the release notes, or keep the first five on their old positions.

Decided: Fathom takes Ocean's linear Mix in the plug-in, and the reference's level stage and clipper stay as they are, the clipper behind the Mix. What that leaves: with Mix below 100 % a dry signal above +8 dBFS is turned down in Fathom and in no other Character.
Ocean's defaults (Low Cut 80 Hz, High Damping 9 kHz, Focus 100 %) take Fathom far from the reference. Keep the documented knob moves, or set the three to neutral when Fathom is selected.

Decided: every instance of the plug-in draws a voice seed of its own and does not store it. Left open by it: an export rendered in an instance of its own, a duplicated track and a reopened project sound another movement; an open instance repeats its movement at every restart of processing.
Low Cut and High Damping step at their end stops, and the Low Cut readout reads 20 Hz up to 20.5 Hz. Keep as the price of exact neutrality, or bring the filters in gradually.
Host rates outside 22.05 to 384 kHz are processed as the nearest bound (time and pitch scale). Leave, widen the engine's bounds, or keep Fathom out of such sessions.
Entering Fathom ends a sounding tail within 200 ms and leaving it brings up the FDN's tail: documented behaviour to confirm.
Fathom's wet lies 4.6 to 6.3 dB below Default's and is not matched: a recorded decision with new figures.
Cost: the FDN keeps running behind Fathom, and every instance holds the engine's memory and steps its clocks.

Decided: the words of the editor. The segment selector with its words "Tidal / Swell" is gone; the description block carries the texts the owner approved (Fathom: "MODELLED 16-LINE TIDAL NETWORK", "Evolution brings in the tide"). The reference is named in documents only.
Done: README.md is up to date for this revision. Left as it was on the owner's instruction: its list of render fingerprints, which holds four Characters of version 0.8.3.
Done: the clock sign pairs of 64 kHz (low, low) and 384 kHz (high, low) are in the campaign's measured table. SPEC.md still lists the six pairs of wave 2 as measured; it was not edited.

Small text in the deep blue: the label of a toggle that is on reads 4.21 : 1 for Fathom, under the 4.5 : 1 of small text; the word OCEAN reads 4.47 : 1. Keep #2F7FE0 there, or use a lighter tint of the accent for small text.

The calm pool of the GPU background is much wider than the description block (its margin is 0.30 of the frame's height), and the EVOLUTION label outside the block has a glyph pixel under 4.5 : 1 in 15 % of frames at factory settings. Drawing the margin in would bring the field back round the knob and would take from that label the ground it has from standing near the pool (not measured); limiting the field under labels or giving labels a ground of their own is the other way. Nothing was changed.

Space on the drop-down opens the list, as asked. The drop-down has the keyboard as soon as the editor's window has it, so in a host that offers keys to the plug-in first, Space would open the list instead of reaching the transport. No host was run. Keep Space, or leave the list to Return.

The working name survives in four numbers (FathomEngine::defaultVoiceSeed = 0x45626245, which is the text EbbE, and three seeds of test and benchmark noise), in the names of the build folders and in a note of the campaign's emit_engine_constants.py and engine_golden.json. Changing the numbers changes renders, test stimuli and a benchmark checksum. Kept.

Recorded choices of the editor's engineers to confirm or change: the border of the engaged drop-down at 86 % of the accent for all Characters; the drop-down at y 112 where the mock-up said about 110; the foot of the Evolution value taken as the baseline of its text; the keyboard's order, which now goes from the drop-down to the knobs and then to Mono Safe and Freeze, where before it went to the two toggles first.
